name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER10_MATCH_Q01 - Plant tissue culture terms and definitions

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-IList-II
(A) Explant(I) Capacity to generate a whole plant from any cell or explant
(B) Totipotency(II) Part of a plant excised and grown in vitro under sterile conditions
(C) Somaclones(III) Method of producing thousands of plants in very short durations
(D) Micro-propagation(IV) Plants that are genetically identical to the original parent plant

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Pairing for Explant
An explant is biologically defined as any excised tissue, cell, or organ taken out from a plant and inoculated onto a nutrient medium in a sterile test tube to initiate tissue culture.

Step 2: Pairing for Totipotency
Totipotency represents the cellular developmental capability of an isolated somatic cell or explant to regenerate into a complete, fertile whole plant.

Step 3: Pairing for Somaclones
Somaclones are populations of plants regenerated vegetatively via tissue culture that possess identical genetic makeups to each other and to the donor plant from which they originated.

Step 4: Pairing for Micro-propagation
Micro-propagation is the tissue culture methodology applied to produce thousands of clonal plantlets rapidly within very short time intervals.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Combining these pairs establishes the correct relationship: (A) aligns with (II), (B) aligns with (I), (C) aligns with (IV), and (D) aligns with (III). Hence, the correct answer is (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER10_MATCH_Q02 - Agricultural biotechnology agents and targeted pests

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-IList-II
(A) cryIAb(I) Produces insecticidal protein crystals containing protoxin
(B) cryIAc and cryIIAb(II) Specifically controls corn borer
(C) Meloidogyne incognita(III) Specifically controls cotton bollworms
(D) Bacillus thuringiensis(IV) Nematode parasitising roots of tobacco plants

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Pairing for cryIAb
The crystal protein encoded by the specific transgene cryIAb confers insecticidal resistance against the European corn borer in transgenic corn varieties.

Step 2: Pairing for cryIAc and cryIIAb
The specific endotoxins synthesized by the genes cryIAc and cryIIAb confer targeted lethality against lepidopteran cotton bollworms in Bt cotton crops.

Step 3: Pairing for Meloidogyne incognita
Meloidogyne incognita is a parasitic root-knot nematode that infects the root system of tobacco plants, severely reducing crop productivity.

Step 4: Pairing for Bacillus thuringiensis
Bacillus thuringiensis is a soil-dwelling bacterium that forms parasporal protein crystal inclusions harboring insecticidal delta-endotoxin protoxins during sporulation.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual alignment pairs (A) with (II), (B) with (III), (C) with (IV), and (D) with (I). Thus, the correct matching option is (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER10_MATCH_Q03 - Insect taxonomic orders and Bt targeted pests

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Taxonomic Order)List-II (Representative Pests / Organisms)
(A) Lepidopterans(I) Beetles
(B) Coleopterans(II) Tobacco budworm and armyworm
(C) Dipterans(III) Root-knot parasite Meloidogyne
(D) Nematodes(IV) Flies and mosquitoes

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Pairing for Lepidopterans
Lepidopterans comprise butterflies and moths; in agricultural biotechnology, the representative insect pests cited are tobacco budworm and armyworm.

Step 2: Pairing for Coleopterans
Coleopterans constitute the order of beetles, which are targeted by specific classes of Bacillus thuringiensis crystalline endotoxins.

Step 3: Pairing for Dipterans
Dipterans encompass two-winged true flies, with representative examples in the NCERT text being flies and mosquitoes.

Step 4: Pairing for Nematodes
Nematodes are roundworms, exemplified by the root-knot endoparasite Meloidogyne incognita which damages tobacco crops.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Aligning each taxonomic order with its representative organism yields: (A) matches with (II), (B) matches with (I), (C) matches with (IV), and (D) matches with (III). Hence, the correct answer is (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER10_MATCH_Q04 - Therapeutic biological products and their medical applications

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Biological Product)List-II (Application / Clinical Use)
(A) \(\alpha\)-1-antitrypsin(I) Protein enrichment of milk in transgenic cow Rosie
(B) Human \(\alpha\)-lactalbumin(II) Treatment of human emphysema
(C) Functional ADA cDNA(III) Management of adult-onset diabetes
(D) Recombinant insulin chains(IV) Treatment of severe combined immunodeficiency

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Pairing for Alpha-1-antitrypsin
Human alpha-1-antitrypsin is a biological antiprotease product synthesized by transgenic animals to manage and treat emphysema.

Step 2: Pairing for Human Alpha-lactalbumin
Human alpha-lactalbumin is the primary recombinant protein secreted at 2.4 g/L in the milk of the first transgenic cow, Rosie, providing balanced infant nutrition.

Step 3: Pairing for Functional ADA cDNA
Functional adenosine deaminase (ADA) cDNA is transferred via retroviral vectors into lymphocytes to treat hereditary severe combined immunodeficiency caused by ADA deficiency.

Step 4: Pairing for Recombinant Insulin Chains
Recombinant human insulin chains A and B are produced in bacterial culture and combined via disulfide bonds to manage adult-onset diabetes mellitus.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The correct correspondence maps (A) to (II), (B) to (I), (C) to (IV), and (D) to (III). Therefore, the correct matching option is (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER10_MATCH_Q05 - Diagnostic methods and their operational principles

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Diagnostic Technique)List-II (Operating Principle / Feature)
(A) Polymerase Chain Reaction(I) Based strictly on antigen-antibody interactions
(B) ELISA(II) Conventional method where early detection is not possible
(C) Radioactive nucleic acid probe(III) Clones with mutated genes fail to appear on photographic film
(D) Serum and urine analysis(IV) Amplification of nucleic acid to detect minute pathogen titers

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Pairing for Polymerase Chain Reaction
PCR operates by enzymatically amplifying trace quantities of microbial DNA or RNA, enabling sensitive early diagnosis of pathogens before overt symptoms emerge.

Step 2: Pairing for ELISA
Enzyme-Linked Immuno-sorbent Assay (ELISA) is built upon the specific immunological principle of antigen-antibody interaction to detect pathogen antigens or host antibodies.

Step 3: Pairing for Radioactive Nucleic Acid Probe
A single-stranded radioactive probe hybridizes only to perfectly complementary normal sequences; mismatch due to gene mutation prevents annealing, causing the mutated clone to be absent on photographic film during autoradiography.

Step 4: Pairing for Serum and Urine Analysis
Serum and urine analysis represent conventional clinical diagnostic assays which are incapable of early disease detection because pathogen titers must already be high.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Matching these items results in (A) paired with (IV), (B) paired with (I), (C) paired with (III), and (D) paired with (II). Therefore, the correct matching option is (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(II).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER10_MATCH_Q06 - Structural components and processing of insulin

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Structural Component)List-II (Biochemical Characteristic)
(A) Chain A(I) Connecting peptide removed during proinsulin maturation
(B) Chain B(II) Short polypeptide chain containing 21 amino acids
(C) C peptide(III) Covalent bonds linking chain A and chain B together
(D) Disulphide bridges(IV) Short polypeptide chain containing 30 amino acids

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Pairing for Chain A
In mature insulin, chain A is the shorter polypeptide subunit consisting of exactly 21 amino acid residues.

Step 2: Pairing for Chain B
Chain B is the longer polypeptide subunit in mature human insulin consisting of 30 amino acid residues.

Step 3: Pairing for C Peptide
The C peptide is an extra polypeptide segment present in the prohormone proinsulin that is enzymatically excised and is absent in mature functional insulin.

Step 4: Pairing for Disulphide Bridges
Interchain and intrachain covalent disulphide bridges stabilize and link chains A and B to form the active quaternary hormone structure.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The correct associations are (A) with (II), (B) with (IV), (C) with (I), and (D) with (III). Hence, the correct answer is (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(III).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER10_MATCH_Q07 - Regulatory bodies companies and biological milestones

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-IList-II
(A) GEAC(I) First transgenic cow producing human alpha-lactalbumin enriched milk
(B) Eli Lilly(II) Evaluates validity of GM research and safety of GMO release in India
(C) Rosie(III) Prepared separate DNA sequences for insulin chains A and B in 1983
(D) Indian Patents Bill amendment(IV) Incorporates emergency provisions, research, and development terms

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Pairing for GEAC
The Genetic Engineering Approval Committee (GEAC) is the Indian regulatory body responsible for assessing the scientific validity of genetic engineering research and authorizing the safe introduction of GMOs for public use.

Step 2: Pairing for Eli Lilly
Eli Lilly is the American pharmaceutical enterprise that in 1983 engineered two distinct DNA sequences corresponding to human insulin chains A and B and cloned them separately in E. coli.

Step 3: Pairing for Rosie
Rosie was the pioneering transgenic cow generated in 1997 whose milk yielded 2.4 g/L of human alpha-lactalbumin.

Step 4: Pairing for Indian Patents Bill Amendment
The second amendment of the Indian Patents Bill cleared by Parliament includes terms on emergency provisions, patent durations, and research and development initiatives.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Aligning the organizations and milestones yields: (A) pairs with (II), (B) pairs with (III), (C) pairs with (I), and (D) pairs with (IV). Thus, the correct matching option is (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER10_MATCH_Q08 - Approaches to ADA deficiency treatment and curative potential

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Therapeutic Approach)List-II (Therapeutic Nature / Outcome)
(A) Enzyme replacement therapy(I) Injection of functional adenosine deaminase enzyme to the patient
(B) Bone marrow transplantation(II) Curative approach in some children but not universally permanent
(C) Cultured lymphocyte gene delivery(III) Requires periodic infusion because lymphocytes have a finite lifespan
(D) Gene introduction at early embryonic stages(IV) Can provide a permanent, lifelong cure for ADA deficiency

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Pairing for Enzyme Replacement Therapy
Enzyme replacement therapy involves regular intravenous or intramuscular injections of purified functional adenosine deaminase protein, offering temporary symptom alleviation.

Step 2: Pairing for Bone Marrow Transplantation
Bone marrow transplantation can cure ADA deficiency in some pediatric patients by supplying normal donor hematopoietic precursors, though immune rejection and graft failure represent critical limitations.

Step 3: Pairing for Cultured Lymphocyte Gene Delivery
Transducing peripheral blood lymphocytes with functional ADA cDNA using retroviral vectors requires periodic repeat infusions because mature T-lymphocytes are mortal and eventually die.

Step 4: Pairing for Gene Introduction at Early Embryonic Stages
Introducing the functional ADA gene into cells during early embryonic development ensures that all progenitor stem cell lineages perpetually inherit and express the gene, yielding a permanent cure.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The correct pairs correspond to (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), and (D)-(IV). Therefore, the correct matching option is (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER10_MATCH_Q09 - Timeline of historic discoveries and biotechnology advances

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Year / Decade)List-II (Historical Milestone)
(A) 1950s(I) Production of the first transgenic cow, Rosie
(B) 1983(II) First clinical gene therapy given to a 4-year-old girl with ADA deficiency
(C) 1990(III) Preparation of DNA sequences for insulin chains A and B by Eli Lilly
(D) 1997(IV) Discovery that whole plants could be regenerated from explants

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Pairing for 1950s
During the 1950s, plant physiologists demonstrated that whole plants could be regenerated in vitro from explants, establishing the concept of plant totipotency.

Step 2: Pairing for 1983
In 1983, the American pharmaceutical company Eli Lilly prepared synthetic DNA sequences corresponding to chains A and B of human insulin and expressed them in E. coli.

Step 3: Pairing for 1990
In 1990, the first clinical trial of human somatic gene therapy was administered to a 4-year-old girl suffering from adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency.

Step 4: Pairing for 1997
In 1997, the first transgenic cow, Rosie, was produced; in the same year, patent rights on Basmati rice were granted to an American company by the US Patent and Trademark Office.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Aligning the chronological periods with the biological discoveries produces: (A) corresponds to (IV), (B) corresponds to (III), (C) corresponds to (II), and (D) corresponds to (I). Thus, the correct matching option is (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER10_MATCH_Q10 - Bioresources biopiracy and socioeconomic asymmetry

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-IList-II
(A) Basmati rice(I) Financially wealthy but relatively poor in biodiversity and traditional knowledge
(B) Biopiracy(II) Rich in biodiversity and traditional knowledge related to bio-resources
(C) Developing nations(III) Distinct for unique aroma with 27 documented varieties grown in India
(D) Industrialized nations(IV) Unauthorized exploitation of bio-resources without compensatory payment

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Pairing for Basmati Rice
Basmati rice is celebrated for its unique aroma and flavor, with 27 documented indigenous varieties cultivated in India.

Step 2: Pairing for Biopiracy
Biopiracy refers to the unauthorized use and patenting of bio-resources and traditional indigenous knowledge by multinational corporations without consent or compensatory benefit sharing.

Step 3: Pairing for Developing Nations
Developing and underdeveloped countries are typically rich in biodiversity and indigenous traditional knowledge concerning biological resources.

Step 4: Pairing for Industrialized Nations
Most industrialized nations are financially and technologically prosperous but comparatively poor in native biodiversity and traditional ecological knowledge.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Combining these pairs maps (A) to (III), (B) to (IV), (C) to (II), and (D) to (I). Therefore, the correct matching option is (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).
